transcript: One of my biggest theater regrets of last year is missing Cold War Choir practice during its initial off Broadway run. It completely sold out its initial run. I was not able to get a ticket, and I was really sad about it because I had heard really good things, which is why I was so excited when I heard that MCC was bringing it back this year as a part of their current season. And I am making this video so that you do not make the same mistake that I made last year. And you can get tickets to this before it sells out again, and it is only playing through the end of the month. So let me tell you what it's about. Cold War Choir Practice is about a young girl named Meek growing up during the Cold War. The show is first and foremost a comedy, although it does blend in a bunch of other genres ranging from, like, political spy thriller to family drama. And while it's not a musical, there are many satirical songs throughout. It's almost cabaret esque, where the songs are a commentary on the social climate of the time. And while in lesser hands, I do think these tones could clash here, it never feels disjointed. It creates this really unique, off kilter tone that manages to keep you both on the edge of your seat and also sufficiently entertained throughout. And also it has Grace Mcclain in it, so That just makes any show a must see in my book. It's closing at the end of the month, March 29. So if you're around at all this month, I definitely recommend checking this one out.
